RULES: ES module, Node built-ins only (`node:test`, `node:assert/strict`). Use the fake browser in `/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs` — READ IT FIRST: `loadApp()` returns a page with `page.el(id)` (test-side FakeElement: .tag, .childNodes, .children, .value (settable by test), .disabled, .type, .textContent, .dispatch(type) → event {defaultPrevented, preventDefaultCalls}, .click()), `page.fetches` (FetchCall: .url, .options, .method, .reply(status, body) — body undefined makes json() reject, .replyNotJson(status), .replyLater(status) → {send(body), fail()}, .fail()), `page.listFetches()`, `page.lastFetch()`, `page.log` (ordered strings of every set/call the script made: '#book.disabled=false', '#title.value=""', '#error.textContent="x"', 'fetch GET /api/bookings', 'response.json()', '<button>.disabled=true' ...), `page.violations` (must be [] in every test), `flush()`, `describeChildren`. Do NOT edit helpers or public/. Write local helpers (e.g. `boot(bookings)` that loads, answers rooms 200 {rooms:[Aurora,Borealis,Cosmos]} and the list, flushes; `fillForm(page, values)`; `cancelButton(page, index)` = page.el('booking-list').children[index].children[0]). Exact equality (strictEqual/deepStrictEqual), never prefix/regex. End every test with `assert.deepStrictEqual(page.violations, [])`. No console.log. File ≤ 450 lines, functions < 50 lines. Run `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2 && node --test test/app-submit-cancel.test.mjs` until passing. If a test fails on the real app.js and the spec clearly says otherwise, do NOT weaken it: keep it and report it with repro.

Spec excerpt (full: /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/.team/notes/spec.md section Page; contract .team/notes/page.md):
- Error status = status other than the success status (201 for POST, 204 for DELETE, 200 GET). Error message = body.error when body is a JSON object with string `error`, else `Request failed.`. A non-204 reply whose body cannot be read or parsed as JSON counts as no reply. No reply → #error `Could not reach the server.`.
- Booking: a submit event never reloads the page (preventDefault). A submit while `Book` is disabled sends nothing. Otherwise the script disables Book, then sends POST /api/bookings with exactly the header `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON body whose keys room, title, date, start, end hold the five controls' current values unchanged (title not trimmed). The script never checks the fields itself. Book is enabled again as soon as the request settles (the reply and its body have arrived, or the request failed), before anything else happens. On 201 the title control is emptied (others keep values), #error emptied and the list fetched again. On any other status #error shows the reply's error message exactly. With no reply #error shows `Could not reach the server.`. In both of these cases form and list stay as they were.
- Cancel: clicking a Cancel button disables it and sends DELETE /api/bookings/<id>; the button is enabled again when the request settles. On 204 #error is emptied; on any other status #error shows the error message (e.g. `booking not found`). After either, the list is fetched again. With no reply, #error shows `Could not reach the server.` and the list is not fetched again.
- List URL: /api/bookings, plus ?date=<value> while #filter-date value is non-empty. Only the last started list fetch's outcome is used.

Submit tests:
- Request shape: set room.value='Borealis', title '  Team  sync ', date '2026-11-3', start '9:00', end '' → dispatch('submit'): event.preventDefaultCalls === 1; synchronously a new fetch: url '/api/bookings', options keys exactly method/headers/body (Object.keys sorted deepStrictEqual ['body','headers','method']), method 'POST', headers deepStrictEqual {'Content-Type':'application/json'}, JSON.parse(body) deepStrictEqual {room:'Borealis', title:'  Team  sync ', date:'2026-11-3', start:'9:00', end:''}; #book.disabled === true.
- Disabled guard: second submit before the reply → preventDefaultCalls 1 on it too, no new fetch. Book disabled by the test beforehand → submit sends nothing (still preventDefault).
- Book re-enabled first: for each outcome (reply 201 with a booking body, reply 409 {error:'room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00'}, fail(), replyNotJson(201)) record page.log length before settling, settle, flush; entries after that index excluding those starting with 'response.' must start with '#book.disabled=false'.
- Book stays disabled until the body arrives: replyLater(201) → flush → disabled true → send(booking) → flush → false.
- 201: set #error text first via an earlier 409 submit; set filter-date value '2026-11-03'; submit → reply 201 → title value '', room/date/start/end unchanged, #error textContent '', exactly one new list fetch with URL '/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03'.
- Other statuses: 409 above → #error exact message, title unchanged, no new fetch, list childNodes same objects; 400 {error:'title must be 1 to 80 characters'}; 500 {error:'internal error'}; 200 (not 201) {id:1,...} → 'Request failed.'; 415 {error:1} → 'Request failed.'; 400 [] → 'Request failed.'.
- No reply: fail() → 'Could not reach the server.', values unchanged, no list fetch; replyNotJson(201) → same and title NOT emptied; replyLater(201).fail() → same.
- After settling, a new submit sends a new POST.
Cancel tests (boot with bookings ids 7 and 12):
- click second Cancel → its button disabled === true synchronously; new fetch url '/api/bookings/12', method 'DELETE', options.body undefined.
- 204 (use reply(204) with NO body so json() would reject — the app must not need it) → button.disabled false, #error '' (pre-set an error first, e.g. via a failing submit), exactly one new list fetch.
- 404 {error:'booking not found'} → #error 'booking not found', one list refetch; 500 {error:'internal error'} → shown + refetch; 404 'x' → 'Request failed.' + refetch; 200 {} (not 204) → 'Request failed.' + refetch.
- No reply: fail() → 'Could not reach the server.', NO list refetch (fetch count unchanged after flush), button enabled again; replyNotJson(404) → same (no refetch).
- Double click while pending → one DELETE.
- Refetch uses the filter: filter '2026-11-03' → refetch URL '/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03'.
- The cancel refetch obeys "last started wins": cancel → 204 → refetch R; then dispatch filter change → F; answer F [x], then R [y] → list shows x.

Final message: test count, pass/fail, failing-on-real-code tests with repro, line count.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.
